lesson.title: Compare fractions of the same whole
lesson.subtitle: Use equal-whole pictures
lesson.story: Both rectangles are equal-sized wholes. Compare the shaded area in the pictures.
lesson.objective: Compare unit or like fractions of equal-sized wholes.

steps.title: Look at the first whole
steps.prompt: How many parts of Rectangle A are shaded?
hints: Look carefully at the whole picture.
Count the parts in the picture.
Separate the number of shaded parts from the number of all parts.
Count in the picture: there are 1 shaded parts.

steps.title: Look at the second whole
steps.prompt: How many parts of Rectangle B are shaded?
hints: Look carefully at the whole picture.
Count the parts in the picture.
Separate the number of shaded parts from the number of all parts.
Count in the picture: there are 1 shaded parts.

steps.title: Compare the shaded amounts
steps.prompt: Which equal-sized whole has more shaded area?
hints: The two whole rectangles are the same size.
Look at the shaded area in each whole.
For equal-sized parts, count them. For unit fractions, compare the size of one part.
Using the whole picture, choose Rectangle A.

steps.title: Explain your thinking
steps.prompt: What must we check before naming or comparing these fractions?

choices.label: Count the shaded parts, even if the parts are different sizes.
Check that the parts are equal and the wholes are the same size.
A fraction with a bigger denominator is always the bigger one.

hints: Think about what a fraction describes.
Each part must have the same area.
Comparison also needs the same-sized whole.
Check that the parts are equal and the wholes are the same size.
